learning_outcomes.text: Forming the advanced mathematical foundations necessary for the mathematical modeling of physical engineering processes.
Understanding and correct use of the notions of line and surface integrals, equations and systems of differential equations, and the equations of mathematical physics.
Developing calculation capabilities and skills through the use of interdisciplinary connections, efficiently utilizing the indicated specialized bibliography.
Ensuring professional competencies to apply the knowledge acquired through the course topics in solving engineering problems with interdisciplinary connections.

syllabus_topics: Curvilinear integrals of the first and second kind; Curvilinear integral with respect to the arc element. Curvilinear integral with respect to coordinates. Curvilinear integral independent of path. Applications. Green's formula.
Surface integrals of the first and second kind. Surface integrals with respect to the area element and with respect to coordinates. Stokes' formula. Gauss-Ostrogradsky formula. Applications.

First-order differential equations. Cauchy's problem. Differential equations with separable variables and with total differentials. Homogeneous and generalized homogeneous differential equations. First-order linear differential equations.

Higher-order linear differential equations. Homogeneous and non-homogeneous higher-order linear differential equations. Lagrange's method of variation of constants. Linear differential equations with constant coefficients.
Systems of linear differential equations with constant coefficients. Homogeneous and non-homogeneous systems of linear differential equations with constant coefficients.

assessment_methods.method: Practical activities and seminar work (including exercises, written paper, seminar assignments, and attendance)

assessment_rules: The final exam grade is the integer part of (0.6 * Written Exam Grade + 0.4 * Seminar Grade + 0.5). The minimum performance standard requires the ability to describe the fundamental resolution methods presented in the course. No resit arrangements or explicit minimum marks for components are stated.
